# CLAUDE.md Global context for every agent working in this repository (main session and subagents). The rules here are binding. If a rule seems wrong, stop and ask the human; do not work around it. Related files: [FLOW.md](FLOW.md) (the flow, step by step), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (catalogue of agents and skills), [README.md](README.md) (how to run the project). ## 1. Precedence of instructions An explicit instruction from the human in the session overrides everything below, and it must be **recorded** where it applies (spec Review log, ADR, or `tasks.md`) so the decision is traceable. Among the written sources, when two disagree, the higher one wins: 1. **`CLAUDE.md`** (this file) 2. **Accepted ADRs** in `adr/` (status `Accepted`; `Proposed` ADRs are not binding) 3. **Project skills**: skills in `.claude/skills/` written for this project 4. **Third-party skills**: vendored skills listed in `.claude/skills/THIRD_PARTY.md` A third-party skill never overrides a project decision. If one tells you to do something that a higher source forbids or has not yet decided, follow the higher source and note the conflict in your output. ## 2. Language - Everything in the repository is in **English**: code, identifiers, comments, Markdown docs (README, FLOW, specs, ADRs, reviews), commit messages, branch names, PRs, review comments, and agent and skill definitions. - **End-user content is in Spanish**: Strapi seed data (labels, help texts, error messages, plans, coverages, terms and conditions), because the users are in Colombia and Chile. ## 3. Security and data - Never print tokens, secrets or the contents of `.env` files in any output. - `.env` is git-ignored. Only `.env.example` with fictitious values is committed. - Only fictitious data anywhere in the repo (people, documents, plates, cards). - No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser. - Do not use skills, plugins or memory from the user's global `~/.claude`. Everything the flow uses is versioned in this repository. ## 4. Toolchain versions (pinned) | Tool | Version | Rule | |---|---|---| | Angular CLI / framework | **22.3.0** (latest stable, verified on npm on 2026-11-20) | Scaffold with `npx @angular/cli@22.3.0 new …`. **Never use `@latest`** or an unpinned `npx @angular/cli`. Pin exact versions in `package.json` (no `^`/`~` on `@angular/*`). | | Unit tests | Vitest (Angular 22 CLI default) | — | | E2E tests | `@playwright/test` | Do not use `playwright-ng-schematics` unless a human approves it. | Upgrading any pinned version requires an ADR or an explicit human approval recorded in the relevant `tasks.md`. ## 5. Third-party skill overrides These rules override the vendored `angular-developer` skill (see `docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`, EVAL-001): - **Forms strategy is not taken from the skill.** `references/signal-forms.md` says Signal Forms are mandatory. Ignore that: Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms is decided by an ADR after SPIKE-01 (see §7). Until that ADR is accepted, do not write production form code. - **The Angular CLI MCP server is not used.** Do not configure it (`references/mcp.md`) and do not run `npx @angular/cli mcp`. - **The Angular CLI version is pinned** (§4). The skill's "no version / `@latest`" defaults do not apply. - **Naming follows §6**, not the skill's ambiguous examples. - **Keyboard accessibility of the wizard** is enforced by the project `review-checklist` skill. The skill's ARIA guidance is supplementary. - Reads of `angular.dev` are allowed as a reference, but any decision based on them must be written into a spec or ADR. - Never edit vendored skill files. Overrides go here. ## 6. Naming conventions Status: **Accepted** — approved by Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20. The rule is to follow the Angular 22 CLI defaults (no role suffix in file or class names) and to use **intent-revealing names** so the role stays obvious without a suffix. ### Angular (`frontend/`) | Artifact | File | Identifier | Example | |---|---|---|---| | Component | `kebab-case.ts` + `.html` + `.css` (same base name) | `PascalCase`, no `Component` suffix | `plan-list.ts` → `PlanList` | | Routed page (wizard step) | `-page.ts` | `…Page` | `quote-form-page.ts` → `QuoteFormPage` | | Service: HTTP access | `-api.ts` | `…Api` | `country-content-api.ts` → `CountryContentApi` | | Service: signal state | `-store.ts` | `…Store` | `quote-store.ts` → `QuoteStore` | | Guard / interceptor / resolver (functions) | `-guard.ts`, `-interceptor.ts`, `-resolver.ts` | `camelCase` + role | `wizard-step-guard.ts` → `wizardStepGuard` | | Pipe | `-pipe.ts` | `…Pipe`; template name `camelCase` | `masked-document-pipe.ts` → `MaskedDocumentPipe` / `maskedDocument` | | Directive | `.ts` | `PascalCase` | `autofocus-error.ts` → `AutofocusError` | | Types / models | `.model.ts` | `PascalCase` interfaces and types, no `I` prefix | `field-config.model.ts` → `FieldConfig` | | Pure functions | `.ts` | `camelCase` exported functions | `price-rules.ts` → `calculateFinalPrice()` | | Validators | `-validators.ts` | `camelCase` factories | `field-validators.ts` → `legalAge()` | | Unit tests | `.spec.ts` next to the file | `describe(' …')` | `price-rules.spec.ts` | | E2E tests | `frontend/e2e/-.spec.ts` | `test(' …')` | `us-01-03-full-flow-co.spec.ts` | | Component selector prefix | — | `app-` | `app-plan-card` | | Constants and injection tokens | in the file that owns them | `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` | `STRAPI_BASE_URL` | Folders: `src/app/core/` (singletons, API clients, interceptors), `src/app/features//` (wizard steps), `src/app/shared/` (reusable presentational UI, pipes, pure functions). ### Strapi (`backend/`) - Content-type API IDs: singular `kebab-case` (`form-field`, `plan`, `country`, `terms`). - Components: `category.kebab-name` (`form.select-option`, `plan.coverage`). - Attribute names: `camelCase` (`isRecommended`, `sortOrder`, `errorMessage`). - Custom code files: `kebab-case.ts`. ### Repository artifacts - Specs: `specs/US-01/{story,spec,tasks}.md` - ADRs: `adr/NNNN-kebab-title.md` (4-digit, sequential) - Reviews: `reviews/US-01-review-R1.md` - Branches: `feat/us-01-short-slug`, `fix/us-01-…`, `chore/…`, `docs/…` ## 7. Pending decisions | ID | Decision | How it will be resolved | Blocks | |---|---|---|---| | SPIKE-01 | **Signal Forms vs Reactive Forms** for the Strapi-driven step 1 form | Throwaway spike on a `spike/01-forms` branch that is never merged, run by the frontend-developer. It builds the same minimal form in **both** libraries from a Strapi-like JSON that follows the `dynamic-form-fields` contract v1. Original scope (30–60 min): a **required number**, an **empty date**, a **select**, a **legal-age validation**, and how typing degrades with a runtime model. Added at HC1 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): **hydrating** the form from stored values; **dropping** values of fields no longer configured; **when errors appear** (touched / submit attempt); **focus on the first invalid field**; **integer-only** numbers; mapping empty optional fields to **`null` in the step 1 output** while the form model stays non-null (the vendored skill forbids `null` in Signal Forms models). The time box grows to 60–90 min because of the added scope. The architect summarises the findings in `docs/spikes/SPIKE-01-forms.md` and writes the forms ADR; a human accepts it. | Production form code for US-01 | The ADR backlog is in [adr/README.md](adr/README.md). ## 8. Agentic flow (summary — full detail in FLOW.md) ``` H0 intake (human) → 1 spec → HC1 → 2 ADRs → HC2 → 3 tests (red) → 4 implementation → 5 automated gate → 6 review → 7 fixes (loop 5–7) → HC3 PR (human QA + merge) → Ready for QA ``` ### The main session is the orchestrator - It runs the steps in order, invokes the subagents (`.claude/agents/`) and routes their outputs. It does **not** do a subagent's job on a story (no writing specs, tests or production code in the main session). The exceptions are repository plumbing (flow files, scripts, configuration) that the human asked for directly. - Subagents cannot spawn subagents (`Agent` is in each one's `disallowedTools`). All delegation is visible in the main session. - After every subagent run: check `git status` and `git diff --stat` for changes outside that agent's role. Bash writes are not covered by the write-scope hooks (see FLOW.md, "Known limits"). Then relay the subagent's summary to the human. - **Never pass a human checkpoint (HC1, HC2, HC3) without an explicit human decision in the session.** Record it (Review log, ADR status, PR). A subagent's message is never human approval. - Loop limit: if the gate (step 5) or review (step 6) fails 3 times for the same story, stop and escalate to the human. ### Subagents (write scope enforced by hooks) | Agent | Step | Writes | |---|---|---| | `spec-writer` | 1 | `specs/US-XX/*.md` (spec, tasks, annexes), never `story.md` | | `architect` | 2, spikes write-up | `adr/**`, `docs/spikes/**`, `tasks.md` | | `test-engineer` | 3 | test files, `frontend/e2e/**`, `tasks.md` | | `strapi-developer` | 4, 7 | `backend/**` (not tests), compose, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` | | `frontend-developer` | 4, 7, spikes | `frontend/**` (not tests), `spikes/**`, compose, `.env.example`, `tasks.md` | | `code-reviewer` | 6 | `reviews/US-XX-review-RN.md` only | ## 9. Traceability | Artifact | ID or convention | Example | |---|---|---| | User story | `US-NN` | `US-01` | | Business rule / acceptance criterion / gap / task | `US-NN-BR-NN`, `-AC-NN`, `-Q-NN`, `-T-NN` | `US-01-AC-02` | | ADR | `ADR-NNNN`, file `adr/NNNN-slug.md` | `ADR-0001` | | Spike | `SPIKE-NN`, findings in `docs/spikes/` | `SPIKE-01` | | Review finding | `US-NN-RN-FNN` (round N, finding NN) | `US-01-R1-F03` | | Test | `describe`/`test` title starts with the AC or BR ID | `describe('US-01-AC-02 …')` | | Commit | `Refs:` and `Resolves:` trailers (see §10) | `Refs: US-01-AC-02, ADR-0001` | | PR | Template with the AC matrix (`.github/pull_request_template.md`) | — | The chain **US → spec → ADR → commit → test → review → PR** is checked mechanically by `scripts/trace.sh US-NN`. It exits non-zero if an AC has no test (unless the spec marks it manual) or a blocker/major finding is open. ## 10. Git conventions - Branches: see §6 (`feat/us-01-slug`, `spike/01-forms`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`). Spike branches are never merged. - Commits: [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) in English, `type(scope): summary`, with trailers: - `Refs: US-01-AC-02, ADR-0001` (required in `feat`, `fix` and `test` commits of a story) - `Resolves: US-01-R1-F03` (fix commits for review findings) - `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 ` when an agent authored it - Small commits: one task (`US-NN-T-NN`) or one finding per commit where practical. Tests and production code go in separate commits (they come from different agents). - Local identity only (`git config --local`). The author is the human; agents are co-authors. - No pushes to `main`, no force pushes, and no `--no-verify` (enforced by `.claude/hooks/guard-bash.mjs`). Changes reach `main` only through a PR merged by the human. ## 11. Session continuity Follow the `session-handoff` skill at the start and end of every session. The state of each story lives in `specs/US-NN/tasks.md` (*Current step*, *Next action*). Session logs are exported, unedited, to `logs/sessions/`. ## 12. Definition of Done (Ready for QA) A story is **Ready for QA** when all of these hold: - [ ] The spec is `Approved` (HC1), and the ADRs it needs are `Accepted` (HC2). - [ ] Every AC is implemented and has a passing automated test, or a documented manual check. - [ ] Lint, build, unit and e2e pass. `docker compose up` starts the stack with seed data for CO and CL. - [ ] `scripts/trace.sh US-NN` exits 0, and `scripts/scan-secrets.sh` exits 0. - [ ] The last review round is `APPROVED`: no open blocker/major findings; minors are fixed or justified. - [ ] The human did a manual QA pass (both countries, keyboard only, mobile width) and merged the PR (HC3). - [ ] `tasks.md` shows `Ready for QA`, and the session logs are exported. # FLOW — From functional user story to QA handoff This document explains how a user story becomes a QA-ready increment in this repository: who does what (AI agent or human), what each step produces, and where a person approves, rejects or corrects the work. The binding rules live in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). The agent and skill catalogue is in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). --- ## 1. Design choices ### Tool: Claude Code | Need | How Claude Code covers it | |---|---| | Subagents with separate responsibilities, versioned | `.claude/agents/*.md`: instructions, allowed and disallowed tools, model, preloaded skills, hooks | | Reusable project knowledge, versioned | `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` with templates, loaded on demand | | A global context file that governs generation | `CLAUDE.md`, loaded into every session and subagent | | **Enforced** (not just requested) boundaries | `PreToolUse` hooks: per-agent write scopes, a project-wide Bash guard, and permission deny rules for `.env` | | Unedited session logs | JSONL transcripts in `~/.claude/projects/…` plus `/export` | | Git and GitHub from the same agent | Bash with `git` and `gh`, using a repo-local identity and credential helper | Cursor, GitHub Copilot and Codex were alternatives. We did not run a feature-by-feature verification of them, so we make no claims about what they lack. Claude Code was chosen because it covers every row above in one tool, from versioned files, which we verified against its official documentation. The deciding capability is **per-agent tool restrictions plus lifecycle hooks**: they let a human *trust* the separation of responsibilities instead of hoping for it. ### Spec-Driven Development: our own lightweight variant The spec is the source of truth. Tests are derived from it **before** the code, and the code must make them pass. We did not adopt Spec Kit or Kiro, for three reasons: - **Size.** Three stories do not justify their multi-phase scaffolding (constitution, plan and tasks generators). - **Traceability.** We need IDs that run from the story to the PR (`US-01-AC-02`, …). With our own templates (`sdd-spec` skill), every artifact uses them and `scripts/trace.sh` can check them mechanically. - **Gap detection.** The evaluation rewards specs that *detect gaps in the user story*, so our spec template has a first-class **Gaps and open questions** section, where each gap carries a proposed default and a human answer. What we kept from SDD frameworks: spec → plan (ADRs + `tasks.md`) → tasks → implementation, with a human approval between spec and implementation. ### Model allocation | Role | Model | Why | |---|---|---| | Orchestrator (main session) | Claude Opus 5.5 | It holds the whole flow, talks to the human and routes the work | | spec-writer, architect | Claude Opus 5.5 | Judgement-heavy work: finding gaps, weighing alternatives, verifying facts | | test-engineer, strapi-developer, frontend-developer | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | Well-scoped work guided by an approved spec, ADRs and failing tests; faster and cheaper | | code-reviewer | Claude Opus 5.5 | Deliberately a **different model from the implementers**, so the review does not share their blind spots | --- ## 2. Mitigation: the orchestrator checks `git diff --stat` after every subagent; the reviewer flags out-of-role changes; HC3. - **The Bash guard matches patterns.** It catches mistakes, not deliberate obfuscation. The human checkpoints and GitHub branch protection (recommended for a team) remain the real controls. - **Project hooks run only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted** in Claude Code. --- ## 5. Traceability US → spec → ADR → commit → test → review → PR. The IDs and conventions are in `CLAUDE.md` §9–10. Resuming between sessions The state lives only in the repository: `specs/US-NN/tasks.md` (*Current step*, *Next action*), the specs, ADRs and reviews. The `session-handoff` skill defines the start and end procedures, and the end procedure includes exporting the unedited session logs to `logs/sessions/`. --- ## 7. Reflection ### What we would do differently with a team of 5 developers - **Story-level parallelism with clear ownership.** One person owns each story through the flow, and the HC1/HC2 approvers rotate, so nobody approves their own spec or ADR. - **Move the controls to the server.** Branch protection on `main` (required reviews, required checks), CODEOWNERS for `adr/`, `.claude/` and `CLAUDE.md`, and the automated gate (step 5) in CI rather than locally. Local hooks become a convenience, not the control. - **Shared contracts first.** The Strapi content contract and the `FieldConfig` type would become a versioned package or a generated schema, because with five people the frontend and backend drift faster than one orchestrator can catch. - **Changes to the flow go through PRs** with their own review. Changing an agent definition or a skill changes everybody's output. - **A real secret scanner** (for example, gitleaks) in pre-commit and CI, replacing our minimal script. - **Shared, short-lived sessions**: one session per story, with mandatory handoff, so that context never lives in one person's terminal. ### What did not work as expected, and how we adjusted | Issue | What happened | Adjustment | |---|---|---| | Wrong assumption about nested subagents | The initial proposal said subagents cannot spawn subagents. Turn the decisions flagged in a spec's *ADRs needed* into ADRs with **real alternatives**,
honest consequences and verifiable facts, so the human can accept or reject them at HC2.

content.content:
**What it does:** The `status` parameter selects which version of a document the REST API works with. The page says the API "offers the ability to work with the draft or the published version of documents through the `status` parameter." It also applies to write requests, since a `POST` or `PUT` request "publishes immediately unless you pass `status=draft`."

**Default:** `published`. The page states that the "REST API defaults to `published` for every request, including `POST` and `PUT` requests."

**Permissions for `status=draft`:** The page doesn't mention any permission requirement for `status=draft`. The only stated prerequisite is that the "Draft & Publish feature should be enabled."

toolu_01W2KLjM72pgHm8jgvhduoKA.prompt: Quote the exact sentences about: lifetime of sessionStorage (reload, restore, tab close), duplicating a tab, opening a new tab, and scope by origin/protocol.

content.content:
The page doesn't say anything about duplicating a tab, so I've left that out. The closest content is the `opener` bullet, which covers `window.open()`-style opening, not duplication.

**Lifetime (reload, restore, tab close)**
- "The data in `sessionStorage` is only kept for the duration of the page session."
- "A page session lasts as long as the tab or the browser is open, and survives over page reloads and restores."
- "Closing the tab/window ends the session and clears the data in `sessionStorage`."

**Opening a new tab**
- "Opening a page in a new tab or window creates a new session with the value of the top-level browsing context, which differs from how session cookies work."

**Opener relationship (related, not tab duplication)**
- "If the page has an [`opener`], the `sessionStorage` is initially a copy of the opener's `sessionStorage` object. However, they are still separate and changes to one do not affect the other."

**Scope by origin/protocol**
- "`sessionStorage` is similar to `localStorage`; the difference is that while `localStorage` is partitioned by origin only, `sessionStorage` is partitioned by both origin and browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts)."
- "The main document, and all embedded browsing contexts (iframes), are grouped by their origin and each origin has access to its own separate storage area."
- On the exception: "The origin is not a valid scheme/host/port tuple. This can happen if the origin uses the `file:` or `data:` schemes, for example."

The page doesn't use the word "protocol" as a scope rule. It defines origin as a scheme/host/port tuple, so the scheme (protocol) is part of the origin. Pages on `file:` or `data:` origins throw a `SecurityError`.

toolu_01Gvc8ZT75FyyoxNfcfiUxLC.prompt: Quote what the page says about using environment variables in nginx configuration (templates directory, envsubst, NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_DIR, output dir).

content.content:
The page says nginx doesn't handle environment variables in most config blocks by default, but the image adds a function that substitutes them before nginx starts. "Out-of-the-box, nginx doesn't support environment variables inside most configuration blocks."

- **Templates directory:** By default, the function reads files matching `/etc/nginx/templates/*.template`. `NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_DIR` changes this location (default: `/etc/nginx/templates`). If that directory doesn't exist, no template processing happens.
- **Output directory:** Processed files are written to `/etc/nginx/conf.d` by default, controlled by `NGINX_ENVSUBST_OUTPUT_DIR`. "This directory must be writable by the user running a container."
- **Example:** A template line such as `listen ${NGINX_PORT};` becomes `listen 80;` in `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf`.
- **Related settings:** `NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_SUFFIX` sets the template file suffix (default `.template`), and `NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER` takes a regex that limits which variable names are substituted.

- **Output directory:** Processed files are written to `/etc/nginx/conf.d` by default, controlled by `NGINX_ENVSUBST_OUTPUT_DIR`. "This directory must be writable by the user running a container."
- **Example:** A template line such as `listen ${NGINX_PORT};` becomes `listen 80;` in `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf`.
- **Related settings:** `NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_SUFFIX` sets the template file suffix (default `.template`), and `NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER` takes a regex that limits which variable names are substituted.

---
status: Proposed
date: 2026-11-20
decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (approval), architect subagent (proposal)
consulted: specs/US-01/spec.md v0.2 (Approved), specs/US-02/story.md, specs/US-03/story.md, strapi-content-modeling skill, published packages @strapi/core, @strapi/i18n, @strapi/utils 5.63.0 and @angular/router 22.3.0
informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence
---

# ADR-0001: Multi-country content strategy and country context

## Context and Problem Statement

One Angular build serves Colombia and Chile, and every piece of content the wizard shows (form
fields in US-01, plans in US-02, terms and conditions in US-03) differs by country and is edited
by a non-technical business team in Strapi. We must decide (1) how Strapi models which country an
item belongs to and where country-level metadata (currency, number locale) lives, and (2) how the
Angular app knows which country it is running for, including the root address, unknown
countries, switching country (US-01-Q-01, US-01-Q-02) and, folded into this ADR, the wizard step
addresses and the step 2 guard (spec §10 candidate, US-01-Q-19, US-01-Q-27).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07)
- D2. "Content differentiation strategy by country, proposed by you and documented in an ADR" (source: Assessment, multi-country)
- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app; form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment, evaluation); "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment." (source: Assessment, business context)
- D4. "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment, business context). Currency and number format need a per-country home (US-02 story: "The price is shown in the country's currency and format").
- D5. Per-item draft & publish: a single field can be a draft while the rest is published (US-01-AC-13, US-01-Q-24); plans need "published and active" per item (US-02 story).
- D6. The country context must be deep-linkable and testable; root chooser and "Este país no está disponible." (US-01-Q-01 human answer, US-01-AC-17); data never crosses countries (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22).
- D7. Field `key` unique per country (US-01-BR-01, spec §7.1); one request per country configuration (spec §9, performance).
- D8. Step 2 route exists with the AC-19 guard and no page of its own; browser back works per step (US-01-Q-27, US-01-Q-20, US-01-AC-19, US-01-AC-20).
- D9. Public permissions minimal (source: Assessment, security). The model must not force broad read permissions.

## Considered Options

Strapi model (the four options from the `strapi-content-modeling` skill):

1. **A. `country` collection type + `manyToOne` relation** on every per-country type.
2. **B. i18n locales as countries** (`es-CO`, `es-CL`).
3. **C. Enumeration attribute `country`** (`CO`, `CL`) on every per-country type.
4. **D. One document per country** (a `country-config` holding fields and plans as components or dynamic zones).

Country resolution in Angular:

- **R1. Path segment** `/co/…`, `/cl/…`, chooser at `/`.
- **R2. Host name** (`co.example.test`, `cl.example.test`).
- **R3. Query parameter** (`?pais=co`).
- **R4. In-app selector** with the choice kept in storage, no country in the URL.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"A. `country` collection type + relation" with "R1. Path segment"**, because A
is the only model that gives every item its own draft/publish lifecycle (D5) *and* a typed home for
country metadata (D4) without a schema change per country (D3), and R1 makes the country context
explicit, deep-linkable and testable with one build (D1, D6) without DNS or hosts-file setup.

### What is decided

**Strapi model**

- A `country` collection type (API ID `country`, draft & publish on) with: `code` (string,
  required, unique, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 in upper case, `^[A-Z]{2}$`), `name` (Spanish, shown in the
  chooser: "Colombia", "Chile"), `currencyCode` (ISO 4217: `COP`, `CLP`), `locale` (BCP 47 tag used
  for number and currency formatting: `es-CO`, `es-CL`) and `sortOrder` (integer). Later stories
  may add country-level attributes (for example a document masking rule for US-03) through their
  own spec; this ADR fixes only where they live.
- Every per-country content type (`form-field` in US-01; `plan` in US-02; `terms` in US-03) has a
  **required `manyToOne` relation `country`** to `country`. Draft & publish is on for all of them.
- `config/api.ts` sets `documents.strictRelations: true`, so Strapi rejects publishing an item
  whose required `country` relation is empty. Verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
  (`services/document-service/entries.js`, `services/entity-validator/index.js`): required
  relations are enforced only when this flag is `true`, and never for drafts.
- `key` uniqueness **per country** is enforced server-side by a Document Service middleware
  (`strapi.documents.use`, present in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`) or a lifecycle check on
  create/update/publish of `form-field`. Strapi's `unique` is not scoped by relation, so it cannot
  be used for this.
- The front end reads a country's fields in one request:
  `GET /api/form-fields?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&populate[…]&sort=sortOrder:asc&pagination[pageSize]=100`
  (exact `populate` per the US-01 content type). Filtering through the relation needs `find` on
  `country` for the reader (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
  `validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` checks `<target>.find` for relations used in
  filters). That permission is needed anyway for the chooser and is justified in ADR-0002.

**Country context in Angular**

- The **list of supported countries is content**: the published `country` entries, loaded once
  per full page load (`GET /api/countries?sort=sortOrder:asc`, narrow `fields[]`) into a
  `CountryStore`, validated at the boundary (`code` matches `^[A-Z]{2}$`, `name` non-empty,
  `currencyCode` matches `^[A-Z]{3}$`; invalid entries dropped with a `console.warn`). No country
  code, name or list exists in front-end code.
- The URL segment is the lower-case country code. Matching is case-insensitive; a non-canonical
  address (`/CO/datos`) redirects to the canonical lower-case one with `replaceUrl`.
- **Unknown or unpublished country** (`/ar/…`): the page shows the code-owned message "Este país
  no está disponible." and links to each loaded country (AC-17). No field configuration is
  requested. The address is kept as typed (no redirect), so the user sees what they asked for.
- **Root `/`**: country chooser listing the loaded countries as links ("Colombia", "Chile") to
  `/<code>/datos`. No detection from IP or browser locale.
- **Country list cannot be loaded** (Strapi down, timeout): the chooser and the unknown-country
  page show the same load error state as step 1 ("No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de
  nuevo." is form-specific, so the copy for this state is set by the spec; see *Spec impact*) with
  "Reintentar". The app never claims a country is unavailable when it simply could not check.
- **Switching country (US-01-Q-02)**: there is no in-page selector. Switching means opening the
  other country's address (from the chooser or by typing it). Entering a supported country's
  context whose code differs from the country held in the wizard state discards the stored state
  (mechanics in ADR-0003). Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not discard anything.

**Wizard routes and step guards (folded in from the spec §10 candidate)**

| Address | Route content | Guard | Story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | Country chooser page | — | US-01 |
| `/:country` | Parent route of the wizard; `canMatch: [supportedCountryGuard]` | country must be in `CountryStore` | US-01 |
| `/:country` (empty child) | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/datos` | Step 1 page (`QuoteFormPage`) | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/planes` | **No component** in US-01: `children: []` | `canActivate: [wizardStepGuard]` | US-01 registers it; US-02 attaches its page without changing address or guard (US-01-Q-27) |
| `/:country/resumen` | Step 3 page | guard for step 3 (defined by US-03) | US-03 |
| `/:country/**` | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `**` (no supported country matched) | Unknown-country page | — | US-01 |

- Step slugs are Spanish because they are user-visible (same status as the wizard chrome copy in
  US-01-Q-14); identifiers in code stay English.
- A route with `children: []` and no component is valid in `@angular/router@22.3.0`
  (`_router-chunk.mjs`, route validation error 4014 requires one of `component`,
  `loadComponent`, `redirectTo`, `children` or `loadChildren`). `redirectTo` cannot be combined
  with `canActivate`/`canMatch` on the same route (same file), which is why the redirects are
  separate child routes.
- `wizardStepGuard` is a `CanActivateFn` (`@angular/router@22.3.0`: `type CanActivateFn = (route,
  state) => MaybeAsync<GuardResult>`, `GuardResult = boolean | UrlTree | RedirectCommand`). It
  allows step 2 only if the wizard state holds step 1 values **for the route's country** that pass
  the same pure validators against the field configuration loaded in this page load. Otherwise it
  returns `new RedirectCommand(router.parseUrl('/<country>/datos'), { replaceUrl: true })`, so the
  blocked address does not stay in the history (AC-19). If the configuration cannot be loaded, it
  redirects to step 1, which shows the load error state.
- Each step is its own history entry: "Continuar" navigates normally (no `replaceUrl`), so the
  browser back action returns to step 1 (US-01-Q-20, AC-20).
- Focus on step change: the arriving step's heading receives focus (step 1 in US-01; step 2 and 3
  in their stories, spec §8).
- Field configuration and countries are fetched once per full page load and kept in memory for
  that page load only (US-01-Q-16); nothing about content is stored across reloads (ADR-0003).

### Consequences

- Good, because every field, plan and term has its own draft/publish state, ordering and audit
  history in the Strapi admin (D5), and the seed's draft-only `email` field (AC-13) is expressible.
- Good, because currency and number locale have one typed home that US-02 and US-03 reuse (D4).
- Good, because adding a third country is content work (a `country` entry plus its fields, plans
  and terms) with no schema change and no front-end change (D3), unless that country needs new
  code-backed rules.
- Good, because the URL carries the country: deep links, bookmarks, e2e tests and the AC-19 guard
  all work from the address alone (D6, D8).
- Bad, because editors must pick the country on every item; an item saved without one is invalid
  — mitigation: required relation + `strictRelations: true` blocks publishing it, and the
  frontend only queries filtered by country, so an orphan is never shown.
- Bad, because `key` uniqueness per country needs custom server code (Strapi `unique` is global) —
  mitigation: one Document Service middleware with a unit or integration test; the front end also
  drops duplicates at the boundary (AC-14).
- Bad, because there is no editor tool to copy the CO form to CL (i18n would offer "fill from
  another locale") — mitigation: acceptable for two countries; the seed creates both.
- Bad, because the chooser and the unknown-country page now depend on Strapi being reachable —
  mitigation: they show a load error with "Reintentar" instead of a wrong "not available".
- Bad, because the public role needs `find` on `country` in addition to `form-field` — mitigation:
  `country` holds only public, non-sensitive metadata; justified in ADR-0002.
- Neutral: the step 2 address exists in US-01 with an empty content area until US-02 (accepted at
  HC1, US-01-Q-27).

### Confirmation

- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts`: CL fields only in `/cl/datos` (AC-01), `/ar/datos` shows
  the message and both links and makes no `form-fields` request (AC-17), no data across countries
  (AC-22).
- Unit tests: `supported-country-guard.spec.ts` (code matching, case normalisation, unknown code,
  list not loaded) and `wizard-step-guard.spec.ts` (AC-19: no or invalid data → `RedirectCommand`
  to `/<country>/datos` with `replaceUrl`; valid data → `true`; data of another country → redirect).
- Review checklist: no country code, country name or field list literal in `frontend/src`
  (`grep -rnE "'(CO|CL)'" frontend/src` returns only tests and fixtures); every per-country content
  type has a required `country` relation; `config/api.ts` has `strictRelations: true`.
- Seed check: restarting Strapi does not duplicate countries (natural key `code`).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A. `country` collection type + relation

- Good, because per-item draft & publish, ordering and filtering (`filters[country][code][$eq]`).
- Good, because country metadata (currency, locale) is a typed, editable entry.
- Good, because "market" and "language" stay separate concepts.
- Bad, because the relation must be set on each item and enforced (`strictRelations`).
- Bad, because per-country uniqueness of `key` needs custom code.

### B. i18n locales as countries (`es-CO`, `es-CL`)

Both locales exist in Strapi's ISO list (`@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`, `constants/iso-locales.json.js`).

- Good, because Strapi scopes `unique` by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
  `services/entity-validator/validators.js`: the unique query adds `locale`), so `key` is unique
  per country with no custom code.
- Good, because the admin can fill one locale from another (copy CO to CL).
- Bad, because non-localised attributes are **copied to every locale** on save (verified:
  `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0` `services/localizations.js` `syncNonLocalizedAttributes`, called from
  `bootstrap.js`). One wrong "localised" checkbox on `basePrice` and a CO edit overwrites the CL
  price.
- Bad, because it mixes language with market: a country with two languages, or English copy for
  a market, collides with the one-locale-per-country mapping.
- Bad, because there is no natural home for country metadata (currency) other than a separate
  localised single type, so a second mechanism is needed anyway.

### C. Enumeration attribute `country`

- Good, because it is the simplest schema and filter (`filters[country][$eq]=CO`).
- Bad, because adding a country is a schema change, that is, code and a deployment (against D3).
- Bad, because there is no place for currency or locale; they would end up in front-end code,
  which BR-07 forbids.

### D. One document per country (`country-config` with components)

- Good, because one request returns everything for a country.
- Bad, because draft & publish applies to the whole document: one field cannot stay a draft while
  the others are published (breaks AC-13 and the "published and active" plan rule of US-02
  without an extra flag).
- Bad, because reordering, auditing and editing a single field means editing a large document;
  error-prone for non-technical editors.

### R1. Path segment (chosen)

- Good, because deep links, bookmarks and tests address a country directly; works on `localhost`.
- Good, because the guard and the unknown-country state derive from the URL only.
- Bad, because a user can type another country's address; mitigated by Q-02 (switching discards
  the other country's data).

### R2. Host name

- Good, because it looks natural for country sites.
- Bad, because local `docker compose up` would need hosts-file or wildcard DNS setup, against the
  single-command start (Assessment, environment).

### R3. Query parameter

- Good, because it needs no routing change.
- Bad, because it must be propagated on every navigation and is easily lost; it is a weaker key
  for guards and tests.

### R4. In-app selector stored in the browser

- Good, because URLs stay short.
- Bad, because the country is invisible and not linkable; e2e tests must drive the selector; a
  stored choice silently decides which content a user sees.

## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)

1. Spec §7.3 types `country` as `'CO' | 'CL'`. With a content-driven country list it becomes an
   ISO alpha-2 code validated against the loaded countries.
2. Spec §8 has no state for "country list could not be loaded" on the chooser and the
   unknown-country page; its copy needs to be chosen (US-01-Q-14 owns chrome copy).
3. AC-17's links come from Strapi; they are absent while the load error is shown.

  (files cited inline).
- Related ADRs: ADR-0002 (who may read `country` and `form-field`, and how), ADR-0003 (wizard state
  scope per country and clearing on switch), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved).
- Revisit when: a country needs more than one language, a country needs code-backed rules that
  content cannot express, or the business needs to copy whole forms between countries often.

# ADR-0001: Multi-country content strategy and country context

## Context and Problem Statement

One Angular build serves Colombia and Chile, and every piece of content the wizard shows (form
fields in US-01, plans in US-02, terms and conditions in US-03) differs by country and is edited
by a non-technical business team in Strapi. We must decide (1) how Strapi models which country an
item belongs to and where country-level metadata (currency, number locale) lives, and (2) how the
Angular app knows which country it is running for, including the root address, unknown
countries, switching country (US-01-Q-01, US-01-Q-02) and, folded into this ADR, the wizard step
addresses and the step 2 guard (spec §10 candidate, US-01-Q-19, US-01-Q-27).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07)
- D2. "Content differentiation strategy by country, proposed by you and documented in an ADR" (source: Assessment, multi-country)
- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app; form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment, evaluation); "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment." (source: Assessment, business context)
- D4. "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment, business context). Currency and number format need a per-country home (US-02 story: "The price is shown in the country's currency and format").
- D5. Per-item draft & publish: a single field can be a draft while the rest is published (US-01-AC-13, US-01-Q-24); plans need "published and active" per item (US-02 story).
- D6. The country context must be deep-linkable and testable; root chooser and "Este país no está disponible." (US-01-Q-01 human answer, US-01-AC-17); data never crosses countries (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22).
- D7. Field `key` unique per country (US-01-BR-01, spec §7.1); one request per country configuration (spec §9, performance).
- D8. Step 2 route exists with the AC-19 guard and no page of its own; browser back works per step (US-01-Q-27, US-01-Q-20, US-01-AC-19, US-01-AC-20).
- D9. Public permissions minimal (source: Assessment, security). The model must not force broad read permissions.

## Considered Options

Strapi model (the four options from the `strapi-content-modeling` skill):

1. **A. `country` collection type + `manyToOne` relation** on every per-country type.
2. **B. i18n locales as countries** (`es-CO`, `es-CL`).
3. **C. Enumeration attribute `country`** (`CO`, `CL`) on every per-country type.
4. **D. One document per country** (a `country-config` holding fields and plans as components or dynamic zones).

Country resolution in Angular:

- **R1. Path segment** `/co/…`, `/cl/…`, chooser at `/`.
- **R2. Host name** (`co.example.test`, `cl.example.test`).
- **R3. Query parameter** (`?pais=co`).
- **R4. In-app selector** with the choice kept in storage, no country in the URL.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"A. `country` collection type + relation" with "R1. Path segment"**, because A
is the only model that gives every item its own draft/publish lifecycle (D5) *and* a typed home for
country metadata (D4) without a schema change per country (D3), and R1 makes the country context
explicit, deep-linkable and testable with one build (D1, D6) without DNS or hosts-file setup.

### What is decided

**Strapi model**

- A `country` collection type (API ID `country`, draft & publish on) with: `code` (string,
  required, unique, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 in upper case, `^[A-Z]{2}$`), `name` (Spanish, shown in the
  chooser: "Colombia", "Chile"), `currencyCode` (ISO 4217: `COP`, `CLP`), `locale` (BCP 47 tag used
  for number and currency formatting: `es-CO`, `es-CL`) and `sortOrder` (integer). Later stories
  may add country-level attributes (for example a document masking rule for US-03) through their
  own spec; this ADR fixes only where they live.
- Every per-country content type (`form-field` in US-01; `plan` in US-02; `terms` in US-03) has a
  **required `manyToOne` relation `country`** to `country`. Draft & publish is on for all of them.
- `config/api.ts` sets `documents.strictRelations: true`, so Strapi rejects publishing an item
  whose required `country` relation is empty. Verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
  (`services/document-service/entries.js`, `services/entity-validator/index.js`): required
  relations are enforced only when this flag is `true`, and never for drafts.
- `key` uniqueness **per country** is enforced server-side by a Document Service middleware
  (`strapi.documents.use`, present in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`) or a lifecycle check on
  create/update/publish of `form-field`. Strapi's `unique` is not scoped by relation, so it cannot
  be used for this.
- The front end reads a country's fields in one request:
  `GET /api/form-fields?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&populate[…]&sort=sortOrder:asc&pagination[pageSize]=100`
  (exact `populate` per the US-01 content type). Filtering through the relation needs `find` on
  `country` for the reader (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
  `validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` checks `<target>.find` for relations used in
  filters). That permission is needed anyway for the chooser and is justified in ADR-0002.

**Country context in Angular**

- The **list of supported countries is content**: the published `country` entries, loaded once
  per full page load (`GET /api/countries?sort=sortOrder:asc`, narrow `fields[]`) into a
  `CountryStore`, validated at the boundary (`code` matches `^[A-Z]{2}$`, `name` non-empty,
  `currencyCode` matches `^[A-Z]{3}$`; invalid entries dropped with a `console.warn`). No country
  code, name or list exists in front-end code.
- The URL segment is the lower-case country code. Matching is case-insensitive; a non-canonical
  address (`/CO/datos`) redirects to the canonical lower-case one with `replaceUrl`.
- **Unknown or unpublished country** (`/ar/…`): the page shows the code-owned message "Este país
  no está disponible." and links to each loaded country (AC-17). No field configuration is
  requested. The address is kept as typed (no redirect), so the user sees what they asked for.
- **Root `/`**: country chooser listing the loaded countries as links ("Colombia", "Chile") to
  `/<code>/datos`. No detection from IP or browser locale.
- **Country list cannot be loaded** (Strapi down, timeout): the chooser and the unknown-country
  page show the same load error state as step 1 ("No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de
  nuevo." is form-specific, so the copy for this state is set by the spec; see *Spec impact*) with
  "Reintentar". The app never claims a country is unavailable when it simply could not check.
- **Switching country (US-01-Q-02)**: there is no in-page selector. Switching means opening the
  other country's address (from the chooser or by typing it). Entering a supported country's
  context whose code differs from the country held in the wizard state discards the stored state
  (mechanics in ADR-0003). Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not discard anything.

**Wizard routes and step guards (folded in from the spec §10 candidate)**

| Address | Route content | Guard | Story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | Country chooser page | — | US-01 |
| `/:country` | Parent route of the wizard; `canMatch: [supportedCountryGuard]` | country must be in `CountryStore` | US-01 |
| `/:country` (empty child) | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/datos` | Step 1 page (`QuoteFormPage`) | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/planes` | **No component** in US-01: `children: []` | `canActivate: [wizardStepGuard]` | US-01 registers it; US-02 attaches its page without changing address or guard (US-01-Q-27) |
| `/:country/resumen` | Step 3 page | guard for step 3 (defined by US-03) | US-03 |
| `/:country/**` | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `**` (no supported country matched) | Unknown-country page | — | US-01 |

- Step slugs are Spanish because they are user-visible (same status as the wizard chrome copy in
  US-01-Q-14); identifiers in code stay English.
- A route with `children: []` and no component is valid in `@angular/router@22.3.0`
  (`_router-chunk.mjs`, route validation error 4014 requires one of `component`,
  `loadComponent`, `redirectTo`, `children` or `loadChildren`). `redirectTo` cannot be combined
  with `canActivate`/`canMatch` on the same route (same file), which is why the redirects are
  separate child routes.
- `wizardStepGuard` is a `CanActivateFn` (`@angular/router@22.3.0`: `type CanActivateFn = (route,
  state) => MaybeAsync<GuardResult>`, `GuardResult = boolean | UrlTree | RedirectCommand`). It
  allows step 2 only if the wizard state holds step 1 values **for the route's country** that pass
  the same pure validators against the field configuration loaded in this page load. Otherwise it
  returns `new RedirectCommand(router.parseUrl('/<country>/datos'), { replaceUrl: true })`, so the
  blocked address does not stay in the history (AC-19). If the configuration cannot be loaded, it
  redirects to step 1, which shows the load error state.
- Each step is its own history entry: "Continuar" navigates normally (no `replaceUrl`), so the
  browser back action returns to step 1 (US-01-Q-20, AC-20).
- Focus on step change: the arriving step's heading receives focus (step 1 in US-01; step 2 and 3
  in their stories, spec §8).
- Field configuration and countries are fetched once per full page load and kept in memory for
  that page load only (US-01-Q-16); nothing about content is stored across reloads (ADR-0003).

### Consequences

- Good, because every field, plan and term has its own draft/publish state, ordering and audit
  history in the Strapi admin (D5), and the seed's draft-only `email` field (AC-13) is expressible.
- Good, because currency and number locale have one typed home that US-02 and US-03 reuse (D4).
- Good, because adding a third country is content work (a `country` entry plus its fields, plans
  and terms) with no schema change and no front-end change (D3), unless that country needs new
  code-backed rules.
- Good, because the URL carries the country: deep links, bookmarks, e2e tests and the AC-19 guard
  all work from the address alone (D6, D8).
- Bad, because editors must pick the country on every item; an item saved without one is invalid
  — mitigation: required relation + `strictRelations: true` blocks publishing it, and the
  frontend only queries filtered by country, so an orphan is never shown.
- Bad, because `key` uniqueness per country needs custom server code (Strapi `unique` is global) —
  mitigation: one Document Service middleware with a unit or integration test; the front end also
  drops duplicates at the boundary (AC-14).
- Bad, because there is no editor tool to copy the CO form to CL (i18n would offer "fill from
  another locale") — mitigation: acceptable for two countries; the seed creates both.
- Bad, because the chooser and the unknown-country page now depend on Strapi being reachable —
  mitigation: they show a load error with "Reintentar" instead of a wrong "not available".
- Bad, because the public role needs `find` on `country` in addition to `form-field` — mitigation:
  `country` holds only public, non-sensitive metadata; justified in ADR-0002.
- Neutral: the step 2 address exists in US-01 with an empty content area until US-02 (accepted at
  HC1, US-01-Q-27).

- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts`: CL fields only in `/cl/datos` (AC-01), `/ar/datos` shows
  the message and both links and makes no `form-fields` request (AC-17), no data across countries

- Unit tests: `supported-country-guard.spec.ts` (code matching, case normalisation, unknown code,
  list not loaded) and `wizard-step-guard.spec.ts` (AC-19: no or invalid data → `RedirectCommand`
  to `/<country>/datos` with `replaceUrl`; valid data → `true`; data of another country → redirect).

### A. `country` collection type + relation

- Good, because per-item draft & publish, ordering and filtering (`filters[country][code][$eq]`).

- Good, because the admin can fill one locale from another (copy CO to CL).
- Bad, because non-localised attributes are **copied to every locale** on save (verified:

  a market, collides with the one-locale-per-country mapping.
- Bad, because there is no natural home for country metadata (currency) other than a separate
  localised single type, so a second mechanism is needed anyway.

### C. Enumeration attribute `country`

- Bad, because there is no place for currency or locale; they would end up in front-end code,

- Good, because deep links, bookmarks and tests address a country directly; works on `localhost`.

  `GET /api/form-fields?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&populate[…]&sort=sortOrder:asc&pagination[pageSize]=100`
  (exact `populate` per the US-01 content type). Filtering through the relation needs `find` on
  `country` for the reader (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
  `validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` checks `<target>.find` for relations used in
  filters). That permission is needed anyway for the chooser and is justified in ADR-0002.

**Country context in Angular**

- The **list of supported countries is content**: the published `country` entries, loaded once
  per full page load (`GET /api/countries?sort=sortOrder:asc`, narrow `fields[]`) into a
  `CountryStore`, validated at the boundary (`code` matches `^[A-Z]{2}$`, `name` non-empty,
  `currencyCode` matches `^[A-Z]{3}$`; invalid entries dropped with a `console.warn`). No country
  code, name or list exists in front-end code.
- The URL segment is the lower-case country code. Matching is case-insensitive; a non-canonical
  address (`/CO/datos`) redirects to the canonical lower-case one with `replaceUrl`.
- **Unknown or unpublished country** (`/ar/…`): the page shows the code-owned message "Este país
  no está disponible." and links to each loaded country (AC-17). No field configuration is
  requested. The address is kept as typed (no redirect), so the user sees what they asked for.
- **Root `/`**: country chooser listing the loaded countries as links ("Colombia", "Chile") to
  `/<code>/datos`. No detection from IP or browser locale.
- **Country list cannot be loaded** (Strapi down, timeout): the chooser and the unknown-country
  page show the same load error state as step 1 ("No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de
  nuevo." is form-specific, so the copy for this state is set by the spec; see *Spec impact*) with
  "Reintentar". The app never claims a country is unavailable when it simply could not check.
- **Switching country (US-01-Q-02)**: there is no in-page selector. Switching means opening the
  other country's address (from the chooser or by typing it). Entering a supported country's
  context whose code differs from the country held in the wizard state discards the stored state
  (mechanics in ADR-0003). Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not discard anything.

**Wizard routes and step guards (folded in from the spec §10 candidate)**

| Address | Route content | Guard | Story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | Country chooser page | — | US-01 |
| `/:country` | Parent route of the wizard; `canMatch: [supportedCountryGuard]` | country must be in `CountryStore` | US-01 |
| `/:country` (empty child) | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/datos` | Step 1 page (`QuoteFormPage`) | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/planes` | **No component** in US-01: `children: []` | `canActivate: [wizardStepGuard]` | US-01 registers it; US-02 attaches its page without changing address or guard (US-01-Q-27) |
| `/:country/resumen` | Step 3 page | guard for step 3 (defined by US-03) | US-03 |
| `/:country/**` | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `**` (no supported country matched) | Unknown-country page | — | US-01 |

- Step slugs are Spanish because they are user-visible (same status as the wizard chrome copy in
  US-01-Q-14); identifiers in code stay English.
- A route with `children: []` and no component is valid in `@angular/router@22.3.0`
  (`_router-chunk.mjs`, route validation error 4014 requires one of `component`,
  `loadComponent`, `redirectTo`, `children` or `loadChildren`). `redirectTo` cannot be combined
  with `canActivate`/`canMatch` on the same route (same file), which is why the redirects are
  separate child routes.
- `wizardStepGuard` is a `CanActivateFn` (`@angular/router@22.3.0`: `type CanActivateFn = (route,
  state) => MaybeAsync<GuardResult>`, `GuardResult = boolean | UrlTree | RedirectCommand`). It
  allows step 2 only if the wizard state holds step 1 values **for the route's country** that pass
  the same pure validators against the field configuration loaded in this page load. Otherwise it
  returns `new RedirectCommand(router.parseUrl('/<country>/datos'), { replaceUrl: true })`, so the
  blocked address does not stay in the history (AC-19). If the configuration cannot be loaded, it
  redirects to step 1, which shows the load error state.
- Each step is its own history entry: "Continuar" navigates normally (no `replaceUrl`), so the
  browser back action returns to step 1 (US-01-Q-20, AC-20).
- Focus on step change: the arriving step's heading receives focus (step 1 in US-01; step 2 and 3
  in their stories, spec §8).
- Field configuration and countries are fetched once per full page load and kept in memory for
  that page load only (US-01-Q-16); nothing about content is stored across reloads (ADR-0003).

### Consequences

- Good, because every field, plan and term has its own draft/publish state, ordering and audit
  history in the Strapi admin (D5), and the seed's draft-only `email` field (AC-13) is expressible.
- Good, because currency and number locale have one typed home that US-02 and US-03 reuse (D4).
- Good, because adding a third country is content work (a `country` entry plus its fields, plans
  and terms) with no schema change and no front-end change (D3), unless that country needs new
  code-backed rules.
- Good, because the URL carries the country: deep links, bookmarks, e2e tests and the AC-19 guard
  all work from the address alone (D6, D8).
- Bad, because editors must pick the country on every item; an item saved without one is invalid
  — mitigation: required relation + `strictRelations: true` blocks publishing it, and the
  frontend only queries filtered by country, so an orphan is never shown.
- Bad, because `key` uniqueness per country needs custom server code (Strapi `unique` is global) —
  mitigation: one Document Service middleware with a unit or integration test; the front end also
  drops duplicates at the boundary (AC-14).
- Bad, because there is no editor tool to copy the CO form to CL (i18n would offer "fill from
  another locale") — mitigation: acceptable for two countries; the seed creates both.
- Bad, because the chooser and the unknown-country page now depend on Strapi being reachable —
  mitigation: they show a load error with "Reintentar" instead of a wrong "not available".
- Bad, because the public role needs `find` on `country` in addition to `form-field` — mitigation:
  `country` holds only public, non-sensitive metadata; justified in ADR-0002.
- Neutral: the step 2 address exists in US-01 with an empty content area until US-02 (accepted at
  HC1, US-01-Q-27).

### Confirmation

- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts`: CL fields only in `/cl/datos` (AC-01), `/ar/datos` shows
  the message and both links and makes no `form-fields` request (AC-17), no data across countries
  (AC-22).
- Unit tests: `supported-country-guard.spec.ts` (code matching, case normalisation, unknown code,
  list not loaded) and `wizard-step-guard.spec.ts` (AC-19: no or invalid data → `RedirectCommand`
  to `/<country>/datos` with `replaceUrl`; valid data → `true`; data of another country → redirect).
- Review checklist: no country code, country name or field list literal in `frontend/src`
  (`grep -rnE "'(CO|CL)'" frontend/src` returns only tests and fixtures); every per-country content
  type has a required `country` relation; `config/api.ts` has `strictRelations: true`.
- Seed check: restarting Strapi does not duplicate countries (natural key `code`).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A. `country` collection type + relation

- Good, because per-item draft & publish, ordering and filtering (`filters[country][code][$eq]`).
- Good, because country metadata (currency, locale) is a typed, editable entry.
- Good, because "market" and "language" stay separate concepts.
- Bad, because the relation must be set on each item and enforced (`strictRelations`).
- Bad, because per-country uniqueness of `key` needs custom code.

### B. i18n locales as countries (`es-CO`, `es-CL`)

Both locales exist in Strapi's ISO list (`@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`, `constants/iso-locales.json.js`).

- Good, because Strapi scopes `unique` by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
  `services/entity-validator/validators.js`: the unique query adds `locale`), so `key` is unique
  per country with no custom code.
- Good, because the admin can fill one locale from another (copy CO to CL).
- Bad, because non-localised attributes are **copied to every locale** on save (verified:
  `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0` `services/localizations.js` `syncNonLocalizedAttributes`, called from
  `bootstrap.js`). One wrong "localised" checkbox on `basePrice` and a CO edit overwrites the CL
  price.
- Bad, because it mixes language with market: a country with two languages, or English copy for
  a market, collides with the one-locale-per-country mapping.
- Bad, because there is no natural home for country metadata (currency) other than a separate
  localised single type, so a second mechanism is needed anyway.

### C. Enumeration attribute `country`

- Good, because it is the simplest schema and filter (`filters[country][$eq]=CO`).
- Bad, because adding a country is a schema change, that is, code and a deployment (against D3).
- Bad, because there is no place for currency or locale; they would end up in front-end code,
  which BR-07 forbids.

### D. One document per country (`country-config` with components)

- Good, because one request returns everything for a country.
- Bad, because draft & publish applies to the whole document: one field cannot stay a draft while
  the others are published (breaks AC-13 and the "published and active" plan rule of US-02
  without an extra flag).
- Bad, because reordering, auditing and editing a single field means editing a large document;
  error-prone for non-technical editors.

### R1. Path segment (chosen)

- Good, because deep links, bookmarks and tests address a country directly; works on `localhost`.
- Good, because the guard and the unknown-country state derive from the URL only.
- Bad, because a user can type another country's address; mitigated by Q-02 (switching discards
  the other country's data).

### R2. Host name

- Good, because it looks natural for country sites.
- Bad, because local `docker compose up` would need hosts-file or wildcard DNS setup, against the
  single-command start (Assessment, environment).

### R3. Query parameter

- Good, because it needs no routing change.
- Bad, because it must be propagated on every navigation and is easily lost; it is a weaker key
  for guards and tests.

### R4. In-app selector stored in the browser

- Good, because URLs stay short.
- Bad, because the country is invisible and not linkable; e2e tests must drive the selector; a
  stored choice silently decides which content a user sees.

## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)

1. Spec §7.3 types `country` as `'CO' | 'CL'`. With a content-driven country list it becomes an
   ISO alpha-2 code validated against the loaded countries.
2. Spec §8 has no state for "country list could not be loaded" on the chooser and the
   unknown-country page; its copy needs to be chosen (US-01-Q-14 owns chrome copy).
3. AC-17's links come from Strapi; they are absent while the load error is shown.

## More Information

- Verified sources (all on 2026-11-20, packages fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory):
  `@strapi/core@5.63.0`, `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`, `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`, `@angular/router@22.3.0`
  (files cited inline).
- Related ADRs: ADR-0002 (who may read `country` and `form-field`, and how), ADR-0003 (wizard state
  scope per country and clearing on switch), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved).
- Revisit when: a country needs more than one language, a country needs code-backed rules that
  content cannot express, or the business needs to copy whole forms between countries often.

# ADR-0001: Multi-country content strategy and country context

## Context and Problem Statement

One Angular build serves Colombia and Chile, and every piece of content the wizard shows (form
fields in US-01, plans in US-02, terms and conditions in US-03) differs by country and is edited
by a non-technical business team in Strapi. We must decide (1) how Strapi models which country an
item belongs to and where country-level metadata (currency, number locale) lives, and (2) how the
Angular app knows which country it is running for, including the root address, unknown
countries, switching country (US-01-Q-01, US-01-Q-02) and, folded into this ADR, the wizard step
addresses and the step 2 guard (spec §10 candidate, US-01-Q-19, US-01-Q-27).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07)
- D2. "Content differentiation strategy by country, proposed by you and documented in an ADR" (source: Assessment, multi-country)
- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app; form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment, evaluation); "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment." (source: Assessment, business context)
- D4. "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment, business context). Currency and number format need a per-country home (US-02 story: "The price is shown in the country's currency and format").
- D5. Per-item draft & publish: a single field can be a draft while the rest is published (US-01-AC-13, US-01-Q-24); plans need "published and active" per item (US-02 story).
- D6. The country context must be deep-linkable and testable; root chooser and "Este país no está disponible." (US-01-Q-01 human answer, US-01-AC-17); data never crosses countries (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22).
- D7. Field `key` unique per country (US-01-BR-01, spec §7.1); one request per country configuration (spec §9, performance).
- D8. Step 2 route exists with the AC-19 guard and no page of its own; browser back works per step (US-01-Q-27, US-01-Q-20, US-01-AC-19, US-01-AC-20).
- D9. Public permissions minimal (source: Assessment, security). The model must not force broad read permissions.

## Considered Options

Strapi model (the four options from the `strapi-content-modeling` skill):

1. **A. `country` collection type + `manyToOne` relation** on every per-country type.
2. **B. i18n locales as countries** (`es-CO`, `es-CL`).
3. **C. Enumeration attribute `country`** (`CO`, `CL`) on every per-country type.
4. **D. One document per country** (a `country-config` holding fields and plans as components or dynamic zones).

Country resolution in Angular:

- **R1. Path segment** `/co/…`, `/cl/…`, chooser at `/`.
- **R2. Host name** (`co.example.test`, `cl.example.test`).
- **R3. Query parameter** (`?pais=co`).
- **R4. In-app selector** with the choice kept in storage, no country in the URL.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"A. `country` collection type + relation" with "R1. Path segment"**, because A
is the only model that gives every item its own draft/publish lifecycle (D5) *and* a typed home for
country metadata (D4) without a schema change per country (D3), and R1 makes the country context
explicit, deep-linkable and testable with one build (D1, D6) without DNS or hosts-file setup.

**Strapi model**

- A `country` collection type (API ID `country`, draft & publish on) with: `code` (string,
  required, unique, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 in upper case, `^[A-Z]{2}$`), `name` (Spanish, shown in the
  chooser: "Colombia", "Chile"), `currencyCode` (ISO 4217: `COP`, `CLP`), `locale` (BCP 47 tag used
  for number and currency formatting: `es-CO`, `es-CL`) and `sortOrder` (integer). Later stories
  may add country-level attributes (for example a document masking rule for US-03) through their
  own spec; this ADR fixes only where they live.
- Every per-country content type (`form-field` in US-01; `plan` in US-02; `terms` in US-03) has a
  **required `manyToOne` relation `country`** to `country`. Draft & publish is on for all of them.
- `config/api.ts` sets `documents.strictRelations: true`, so Strapi rejects publishing an item
  whose required `country` relation is empty. Verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
  (`services/document-service/entries.js`, `services/entity-validator/index.js`): required
  relations are enforced only when this flag is `true`, and never for drafts.
- `key` uniqueness **per country** is enforced server-side by a Document Service middleware
  (`strapi.documents.use`, present in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`) or a lifecycle check on
  create/update/publish of `form-field`. Strapi's `unique` is not scoped by relation, so it cannot
  be used for this.
- The front end reads a country's fields in one request:

| `/:country` (empty child) | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/datos` | Step 1 page (`QuoteFormPage`) | — | US-01 |

| `/:country/resumen` | Step 3 page | guard for step 3 (defined by US-03) | US-03 |
| `/:country/**` | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `**` (no supported country matched) | Unknown-country page | — | US-01 |

  separate child routes.

  allows step 2 only if the wizard state holds step 1 values **for the route's country** that pass
  the same pure validators against the field configuration loaded in this page load. Otherwise it

  redirects to step 1, which shows the load error state.
- Each step is its own history entry: "Continuar" navigates normally (no `replaceUrl`), so the
  browser back action returns to step 1 (US-01-Q-20, AC-20).
- Focus on step change: the arriving step's heading receives focus (step 1 in US-01; step 2 and 3
  in their stories, spec §8).
- Field configuration and countries are fetched once per full page load and kept in memory for
  that page load only (US-01-Q-16); nothing about content is stored across reloads (ADR-0003).

### Consequences

- Good, because every field, plan and term has its own draft/publish state, ordering and audit

- Good, because currency and number locale have one typed home that US-02 and US-03 reuse (D4).
- Good, because adding a third country is content work (a `country` entry plus its fields, plans

  code-backed rules.

- Bad, because the public role needs `find` on `country` in addition to `form-field` — mitigation:
  `country` holds only public, non-sensitive metadata; justified in ADR-0002.
- Neutral: the step 2 address exists in US-01 with an empty content area until US-02 (accepted at
  HC1, US-01-Q-27).

- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts`: CL fields only in `/cl/datos` (AC-01), `/ar/datos` shows
  the message and both links and makes no `form-fields` request (AC-17), no data across countries

- Good, because Strapi scopes `unique` by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`

  localised single type, so a second mechanism is needed anyway.

### C. Enumeration attribute `country`

- Good, because it is the simplest schema and filter (`filters[country][$eq]=CO`).
- Bad, because adding a country is a schema change, that is, code and a deployment (against D3).
- Bad, because there is no place for currency or locale; they would end up in front-end code,
  which BR-07 forbids.

### D. One document per country (`country-config` with components)

- Good, because one request returns everything for a country.
- Bad, because draft & publish applies to the whole document: one field cannot stay a draft while
  the others are published (breaks AC-13 and the "published and active" plan rule of US-02
  without an extra flag).
- Bad, because reordering, auditing and editing a single field means editing a large document;
  error-prone for non-technical editors.

### R1. Path segment (chosen)

- Good, because deep links, bookmarks and tests address a country directly; works on `localhost`.
- Good, because the guard and the unknown-country state derive from the URL only.
- Bad, because a user can type another country's address; mitigated by Q-02 (switching discards
  the other country's data).

### R2. Host name
